                        ( p. 1230 ) P هفتاد haftād [Pehl. & Pārsī haftāt ; Zend haptāiti (fr. haptan ); S. सप्तति ], adj. Seventy. 2) هفتادم haftādum
                        ( p. 1230 ) P هفتادم haftādum [ haftād + um = Zend ma = S. म ], adj. The seventieth. 3) هفته hafta
                        ( p. 1230 ) P هفته hafta (rel. n. fr. haft , q.v.), s.m. A week, seʼnnight (cf. S. saptāha ); — the seventh day; Saturday: — hafta-dost , s.m.f. 'A week's acquaintance,' a slight acquaintance; — an inconstant friend: — hafte jaṛnā , To interlock arms (in wrestling): — hafte-kā din , s.m. Saturday. Search Form • DDSA Close

A Dictionary of Urdu, Classical Hindi, and English. A Dictionary of Urdu, Classical Hindi, and English. Search for headword: 'dāī' 35 results Highlight text and press "t" to transliterate (devanagari script only) 1) دي dai, daʼe
                        ( p. 555 ) P دي dai , daʼe [Zend dadhvāʼo , porf. part. act. fr. rt. dā = S. धा , s.m. The tenth month of the solar year (when the sun is in the sign Capricorn), December; the beginning of winter, winter. 2) ديا daiyā
                        ( p. 555 ) H ديا दैया daiyā [Prk. दत्तिओ ; S. दात्रिका ], s.f. Mother; — the stand that children run to in playing hide and seek: — daiyā-dahāṛ or dhāṛ , s.f. 'A cry for mother'; a cry for help; a loud noise, outcry. 3) ديبي daibī
                        ( p. 555 ) H ديبي दैबी daibī , adj. & adv. = daivī , q.v. 4) ديت daiyat, dait
                        ( p. 555 ) H ديت दैयत daiyat , दैत dait , s.m. = ديتيه daitya , q.v. 5) ديتن daitan
                        ( p. 555 ) H ديتن दैतन daitan (Braj), s.m. pl. of dait = daitya : — daitan-bandheo , s.m. 'Binder of the Daityas,' an epithet of Vishṇu. 6) ديتيه daiteya
                        ( p. 556 ) S ديتيه दैतेय daiteya (fr. diti ), s.m. A son of Diti , &c. ( = daitya , q.v.); — adj. Proceeding from or belonging to the Daiteyas; sprung from Diti. 7) ديتيه daitya
                        ( p. 556 ) S ديتيه दैत्य daitya , s.m. 'A son of Diti,' a being hostile to the gods, a demon, an evil spirit, a Titan, giant (of the Hindū mythology): — daitya-yug , s.m. An age of the demons (consisting of 12,000 divine years or the sum of the four Yugas or ages of man): — daitya-yoni , s.m.f. The place or source of demons. 8) ديجور daijūr
                        ( p. 556 ) P ديجور daijūr (fr. A. dāj , rt. دجو 'to be dark,' by imāla +P. aff. war or ūr ; — A. also daijūr ), adj. & s.m. Dark, pitch dark, black; — the night of conjunction of sun and moon; a dark night without moonlight; — anything black; darkness, obscurity. 9) دير dair
                        ( p. 556 ) A دير dair , s.m. A convent or monastery (of Christians, or of Sūfīs, &c.); a temple, a place of worship, a church. 10) ديري dairī
                        ( p. 557 ) P ديري dairī (rel. n. fr. A. dair ), adj. Of or appertaining to an idol temple, &c. (see dair ). 11) ديڙ daiyar
                        ( p. 557 ) H ديڙ दैयड़ daiyar , s.m. = daheṛ , q.v. 12) دين dain, den
                        ( p. 558 ) A دين dain , vulg. den , s.m. A debt; a loan (syn. qarẓ ): — dain-tamassukī , s.f. The certificate given to a banker who has given up his effects: — dain-dār , s.m. A debtor, ower (of, - kā ): — daīn-ě-muʼajjal , s.m. A debt payable on demand: — dain-ě-muwajjal , s.m. A debt of which payment is deferred. 13) دين dain
                        ( p. 558 ) S دين दैन dain (fr. दिन ), adj. Relating to a day, diurnal, daily. 14) دين dain
                        ( p. 558 ) S دين दैन dain (fr. दीन ), s.m. Poverty, wretchedness, misery, miserable condition; humbleness, lowliness; meanness; covetousness. 15) دينت daiṅt
                        ( p. 558 ) H دينت दैंत daiṅt , s.m. = dait , daitya , q.v. 16) دينك dainik
                        ( p. 558 ) S دينك दैनिक dainik (fr. दिन ), adj. Diurnal, daily ( = dain ). 17) دينکي dainikī
                        ( p. 558 ) S دينکي दैनिकी dainikī , s.f. A day's hire or wages. 18) دينيه dainya
                        ( p. 558 ) S دينيه दैन्य dainya (fr. दीन ), s.m. Poverty, &c. ( = dain , and dīnatā , qq.v.). 19) ديو daiv, daʼīv
                        ( p. 559 ) S ديو दैव daiv , vulg. daʼīv , adj. (f. - ī ), Of or belonging to a deity or divinity; coming from the gods, divine, celestial; — s.m. One of the forms of marriage, the gift of a daughter at a sacrifice to the officiating priest; — a deity, a celestial being; — a religious offering or rite, an oblation or offering to the gods; — divine power, destiny, fate, fortune, chance, accident; the part of the hand sacred to the gods, i.e. the tips of the fingers: — daiv-āgat or āgati , s.f. Providential dispensation, sudden misfortune, unforeseen disaster, accident: — daiva-jna , vulg. daivaggya , adj. & s.m. (f. - ā ), Acquainted with fate, knowing the destinies of men, foretelling; — an astrologer, fortune-teller; a prophet: — daiv-jnān , vulg. daiv-gyān , s.m. Knowledge of the destinies of men, supernatural knowledge: — daiv-ćintā , s.f. Reliance on fate, fatalism: — daiv-ćintak , s.m. (f. - ikā ), An astrologer; a fatalist: — dair-saṅyog , adj. Connected with a deity, or with fate: — daiv-karm , s.m. Offering oblations to the gods, sacrificing, worship of the gods, a religious rite ( = dev-karm ): — daiv-gati , daiv-ghaṭnā , s.f. Course of destiny, run of fate, an event for which the gods (rather than men) are answerable, fortune, lot; misfortune, accident: — daiv-lekhak , s.m. (f. - ikā ), An astrologer, a fortune-teller: — daiv-vāṇī , s.f. A voice from heaven, oracle, divine revelation: — daivodyān , s.m. = devodyān , q.v.s.v. deva , dev : — daiv-yug , s.m. An age of the gods, cycle of the immortals: — dair-yog , s.m. A fortuitous combination, the intervention of destiny, the occurrence of any unforeseen event, fortune, chance, accident, contingency: — daiv-yogya , adj. Worthy of chance or fortune. 20) ديوات daivāt
                        ( p. 559 ) S ديوات दैवात daivāt (ablat. of दैव ), adv. By the interposition of fate, fatally, providentially, by chance, fortuitously, accidentally. 21) ديواگت daivāgat, devāgat
                        ( p. 559 ) H ديواگت दैवागत daivāgat , देवागत devāgat [S. दैव + आगति ], s.f. See s.v. daiv . 22) ديوت daivat
                        ( p. 560 ) S ديوت दैवत daivat , adj. Of or relating to a god or to the gods, belonging to a deity; divine; s.m. A god, a deity, an idol of a god; the deities: — daivat-pati , s.m. 'Lord of the gods,' an epithet of Indra. 23) ديوث daiyūs̤
                        ( p. 560 ) A ديوث daiyūs̤ (fr. ديث 'to be soft, or easy'), s.m. A wittol, a tame cuckold; one who winks at the adultery of his wife or the fornication of his female relations from interested motives. 24) ديوجن daivajna, daivagya
                        ( p. 560 ) S ديوجن दैवज्ञ daivajna , vulg. daivagya , s.m. See s.v. daiv . 25) ديوس daiyūs
                        ( p. 560 ) A ديوس daiyūs , s.m. = daiyūs̤ , q.v. 26) ديوك daivak
                        ( p. 560 ) S ديوك दैवक daivak , s.m. (f. - ikā ), An astrologer; an almanac-maker. 27) ديوکا daivikā
                        ( p. 560 ) S ديوکا दैविका daivikā , s.f. A female astrologer; an astrologer's wife. 28) ديوگيه daivagya
                        ( p. 560 ) H ديوگيه दैवज्ञ daivagya , s.m. = daivajna , q.v.s.v. daiv . 29) ديوه daiva
                        ( p. 561 ) S ديوه दैव daiva , adj. = daiv , q.v. 30) ديوي daivī
                        ( p. 561 ) H ديوي दैवी daivī [S. दैविका , fr. दैवः ], adj. Divine; wonderful (see daiv ); — s.f. An inevitable accident, &c. ( = daivāgati ); — adv. By chance, &c. at length (see daivāt ): — daivī-gati , s.f. = daivāgati , q.v.s.v. daiv . 31) ديويه daivīya
                        ( p. 561 ) S ديويه दैवीय daivīya , adj. Of or relating to the gods or to fate. 32) ديويه daivya
                        ( p. 561 ) S ديويه दैव्य daivya , s.m. Divine power or effect, fate, fortune, chance. 33) ڐين ḍain
                        ( p. 576 ) H ڐين डैन ḍain [S. डयन 'flying'], s.m. Wing (of a bird). 34) ڐينا ḍainā
                        ( p. 576 ) H ڐينا डैना ḍainā ( = ḍain ), s.m. Wing (of a bird); branch, bough (of a tree). 35) ڐينی ḍainī
                        ( p. 576 ) H ڐينی डैनी ḍainī (from ḍāʼin , q.v.), adj. f. (m. - ā ), Unlucky, &c. (only occurring in the following): — ḍainī uṅglī , s.f. The middle finger. Search Form • DDSA Close
